'''Gerda Claeskens''' is a Belgian [[statistician]]. She is a [[Professor (highest academic rank)|professor]] of statistics in the Faculty of Economics and Business at [[KU Leuven]], associated with the KU Research Centre for Operations Research and Business Statistics (ORSTAT).{{r|ww}}

==Contributions==
Claeskens is an expert in [[nonparametric statistics]] and in [[model selection]], including model averaging. She is known for developing, with [[Nils Lid Hjort]], the [[focused information criterion]] for model selection. With Hjort, she is the author of the book ''Model Selection and Model Averaging'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 2008).{{r|msma}}

==Education and career==
Claeskens earned a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in mathematics at the [[University of Antwerp]] in 1995. In 1999, she earned a master's degree in [[biostatistics]] and Ph.D. in mathematics, at [[Limburgs Universitair Centrum]] (now the University of Hasselt);{{r|cv}} her dissertation, supervised by Marc Aerts, was ''Smoothing Techniques and Bootstrap Methods for Multiparameter Likelihood''.{{r|cv|mgp}} She did postdoctoral research at the [[Australian National University]]. Afterwards, she was an assistant professor at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (from 1999 to 2000) and at [[Texas A&M University]] (from 2000 to 2004). She joined the KU Leuven faculty in 2004, and was promoted to full professor there in 2012.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
In 2004, Claeskens won the Noether Young Scholar Award of the [[American Statistical Association]].{{r|medallion}} 
She is an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isimem}} In 2012 she was elected as a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], and in 2016 she was a Medallion Lecturer for the Institute, speaking about her work on model selection and model averaging.{{r|medallion}}
In 2019 she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}}
